meta.note: Delta J_cc is a relative shift in an inferred CPM parameter (tau matcher median, q25-q75), not a physical measurement. High J_cc = looser/less cohesive; low = more compact. Only MEKi clears the significance heuristic (n=4). Source: drug_panel_summary.csv.
meta.convention: positive shift = looser spheroid, negative = more compact

classes.target: BTK, in the B-cell receptor (BCR) axis
classes.mech: BTK relays BCR engagement to survival (PLCg2, NF-kB, ERK) and to adhesion/homing signals. Blocking it cuts the microenvironment signal that keeps CLL cells aggregated, and clinically drives cells out of tissue niches.
classes.takeaway: Blocking the BCR at BTK nudges the spheroid looser as predicted, but weakly and non-significantly.

classes.target: SYK, one node above BTK in the BCR axis
classes.mech: SYK sits just downstream of the BCR and phosphorylates BTK/PLCg2, so inhibiting it blocks the same survival and adhesion cascade one step earlier.
classes.takeaway: Same BCR axis as BTKi, but the inferred adhesion shift is small and not significant.

classes.target: PI3K-delta, in the BCR survival / chemokine axis
classes.mech: PI3K-delta carries BCR and chemokine signals to AKT survival and CXCR4 homing. Blocking it strips both the survival and the niche-adhesion signal.
classes.takeaway: Hits the BCR/chemokine axis but produces no clear adhesion shift here.

classes.target: JAK1/2, in the cytokine (JAK-STAT) arm of the stimulus
classes.mech: The IL-2/15/21 activation cocktail signals through JAK-STAT, so JAK inhibition blunts the stimulus itself rather than the BCR, dampening the cytokine push toward the cohesive state.
classes.takeaway: Targets the cytokine arm of the stimulus but leaves inferred adhesion essentially unchanged.

classes.mech: CXCR4 drives homing to protective stromal niches; blocking it mobilizes cells away from the niche. In the model this acts mainly on cell-to-medium (niche) adhesion, not cell-to-cell.
classes.takeaway: Homing blockers scatter both ways on J_cc, fitting the idea that their real target is niche adhesion, not cohesion.

classes.target: MEK1/2 in the MAPK/ERK survival pathway
classes.mech: MEK1/2 relay BCR/RAS signaling to ERK-driven survival. This is mainly a survival probe with a smaller expected adhesion effect than upstream BCR nodes.
classes.takeaway: The only statistically flagged hit, but n=4 (one patient) and pointing to compaction, not the expected weak effect.

classes.target: IKK / NF-kB, a central CLL survival hub
classes.mech: NF-kB integrates BCR, TLR and microenvironment survival signals and is a master anti-apoptotic hub. Blocking it is pro-apoptotic and can shrink the spheroid, so size loss is confounded with apparent adhesion change.
classes.takeaway: A large but borderline negative shift, plausibly entangled with drug-induced shrinkage.

classes.mech: STAT6 carries one narrow cytokine arm; inhibiting it is expected to produce a small, targeted shape change rather than a broad adhesion collapse.
classes.takeaway: A narrow cytokine probe producing only a small, borderline inferred shift.

classes.mech: MALT1 is the paracaspase coupling BCR engagement to NF-kB; inhibiting it disrupts BCR-driven NF-kB survival and is pro-apoptotic, sharing the shrinkage caveat.
classes.takeaway: Blocks BCR-to-NF-kB coupling; inferred adhesion shift is small and non-significant.

classes.mech: Proprietary research compound with no published mechanism, carried as an exploratory arm with no biological prior.
classes.takeaway: Exploratory arm with no mechanism to interpret against; a modest borderline shift.
